meta.title: The Load That Waits for Its Turn
meta.skill_frame: Process: see a step that waits for a count, not for a clock.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 5.80, 5.51 and 5.59 on the three parts (111, 112 and 107 words), 5.63 together. The load is one gate: the count on the cart decides when the machine starts, and a deadline downstream decides when it cannot. The reader must hold both at once.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for process 4.2, band 4.2, sequence 1. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A hospital laundry that runs a washer only when the drum is full, bounded by a six o'clock delivery.
source.avoided: No hospital name, city, machine brand, or cost figure. No claim about how many loads a day runs.

session.difficulty_basis: One step starts on a quantity reached and is bounded by a deadline downstream, so waiting too little and waiting too long cost in different ways.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A hospital laundry sorts dirty linen by color and by weight before anything is washed. Sheets and towels go into one tall cart, and the pale scrubs go into another. The washer does its best work when the drum is full, so the crew checks each cart against a mark painted on the machine. A full drum of sheets is one load, and half a drum of scrubs is also one load. The machine uses the same water, the same soap, and the same hour either way. The crew therefore does not start the machine while the cart is short. It keeps sorting until the cart comes up to the mark.
passage.part_2: The waiting costs the laundry real money, so the crew sorts several hours ahead of the wash. Clean linen has to reach the hospital floors by six in the morning, and one full load takes about an hour from wash to fold. That hour does not shrink when the load is small. A short load consumes the same hour and returns only half the linen. When a cart fills slowly, the crew starts the next load early and sends the scrubs through directly behind the sheets. The mark on the drum determines when the machine starts. The clock on the wall decides when the crew stops waiting and runs what it has.
passage.part_3: The order follows the count, because the count decides whether the next step happens at all. Counting comes before washing, washing comes before drying, and drying comes before folding, since wet linen will not fold. The failure is easy to see. A crew that starts the drum at half a load pays for a full load and dries only half as much. A crew that waits too long misses the six o'clock delivery. The rule is to fill the drum, or to leave it empty and keep sorting the rest. A half load is the one mistake that costs at both ends, in money and in time.

items.prompt: What does the crew compare each cart against?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. A mark painted on the machine.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the crew checks each cart against a mark painted on the machine.
tutor_only.tell: The crew compares each cart with a mark painted on the machine. The mark shows a full drum.
help: The sentence about the washer names what the crew checks each cart against.
It is painted on the machine, not written on the cart.
tutor_only.core_idea: A mark painted on the machine that shows a full drum.
accept_ideas: the line painted on the machine
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the weight of the cart
if_they_say.ask: The passage names a mark, not a scale. What is the cart checked against?

items.prompt: The washer spends the same water, soap, and hour on any load. Why does the crew wait for a full cart?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. A half cart pays for a full load and returns half the linen.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the machine uses the same water, soap, and hour either way, and that a short load returns only half the linen.
tutor_only.tell: A half load spends a full load's water, soap, and hour. It returns half the linen for that cost.
help: The passage says what the machine uses either way.
The same water, soap, and hour, whatever the cart holds.
tutor_only.core_idea: A short load costs the same as a full one and returns only half the linen.
accept_ideas: a half load costs the same and gives half the linen
the machine uses the same water and soap either way
a short load wastes half the water and soap
not_required: how much soap one load takes
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says a half load runs faster
if_they_say.ask: The hour does not shrink for a small load. What does the crew get back?

items.prompt: Clean linen has to be on the hospital floors by six. Why can the crew not wait as long as it takes to fill the drum?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The wait would run past six.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The second part says a full load takes about an hour from wash to fold, and the linen has to reach the floors by six.
tutor_only.tell: A load takes about an hour. Waiting too long for a full drum misses the six o'clock delivery.
help: Two sentences give a time: the six o'clock delivery and the hour a load takes.
An hour from wash to fold, and a six o'clock delivery.
tutor_only.core_idea: Because a full load takes about an hour, so waiting too long misses the six o'clock delivery.
accept_ideas: the load takes an hour and six o'clock comes first
waiting would make the linen late
an hour is needed, so the wait has a limit
not_required: how many carts the hospital sends
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the crew runs out of carts
if_they_say.ask: The carts are not the limit here. What deadline does the linen have?

items.prompt: When carts fill slowly, the crew starts the next load early. Why does the crew give up the full drum?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The delivery time comes first.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage gives a six o'clock delivery and says the hour does not shrink, so the crew runs a short load rather than miss it.
tutor_only.tell: The clock can beat the mark. The crew runs a short load rather than miss the delivery.
help: The crew is trading one rule for another. Which one has a hard deadline?
The mark can wait a morning. The six o'clock cart cannot.
tutor_only.core_idea: The delivery time matters more than a full drum, so the crew runs a short load rather than miss six o'clock.
accept_ideas: the delivery matters more than a full load
it would rather send half than be late
the clock is firmer than the mark
not_required: how often the carts fill slowly
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the crew forgot the mark
if_they_say.ask: The crew knows the mark. What deadline is pressing on it?

items.prompt: A crew starts every load as soon as two carts are half full, so each drum runs half full. What happens to the morning, and why?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Twice the hours for the same linen, so the delivery runs short.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Each half load spends an hour and returns half the linen, so delivering the same linen needs twice the machine hours and the six o'clock cart runs short.
tutor_only.tell: Each half load spends an hour and returns half the linen. Twice the hours are needed, so the delivery runs short.
help: The passage says what a half load spends and what it returns.
One hour and half the linen, on every load of the morning.
tutor_only.core_idea: Each half load spends a full hour and returns half the linen, so the same linen needs twice the hours and the six o'clock delivery runs short.
accept_ideas: twice the hours for the same linen, so the delivery is short
the morning cannot make the same amount of linen
every half load spends an hour and gives half the linen
not_required: how many loads the laundry can run
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the morning stays the same
if_they_say.ask: Nothing in the machine changes for a half load. What does the crew get back for the hour?
